0|480eccf9ae1073b87bb4fe118971fbf134a5bc61|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"Fix NUMA Memory Policy Reference Counting
This patch proposes fixes to the reference counting of memory policy in the
page allocation paths and in show_numa_map().  Extracted from my ""Memory
Policy Cleanups and Enhancements"" series as stand-alone.
Shared policy lookup [shmem] has always added a reference to the policy
but this was never unrefed after page allocation or after formatting the
numa map data.
Default system policy should not require additional ref counting
should the current task's task policy.  However
get_vma_policy() to examine what may be [likely is] another task's policy.
The latter case needs protection against freeing of the policy.
This patch adds a reference count to a mempolicy returned by
get_vma_policy() when the policy is a vma policy or another task's
mempolicy.  Again
column2: shared policy is already reference counted on lookup.  A

column1: matching ""unref"" [__mpol_free()] is performed in alloc_page_vma() for
shared and vma policies
column2: and in show_numa_map() for shared and another

column1: task's mempolicy.  We can call __mpol_free() directly
inexpensive inline NULL test
column2: because we know we have a non-NULL policy.

column1: Handling policy ref counts for hugepages is a bit trickier.
huge_zonelist() returns a zone list that might come from a shared or vma
'BIND policy.  In this case
column2: we should hold the reference until after the

column1: huge page allocation in dequeue_hugepage().  The patch modifies
huge_zonelist() to return a pointer to the mempolicy if it needs to be
unref'd after allocation.
